headline.title: Instagram breakouts continue; TikTok resumes after a 48-day silence.
headline.platformIntro: Instagram produces all of the reach and its breakouts keep coming — two new Xi'an training reels passed 11,888 views — but the newest hits earn very little response. TikTok has posted its first video in 48 days and still barely registers.

executiveSummary: Instagram still produces essentially all of the reach: 197,763 of the 198,754 total views, with a typical post at 312.5 views. TikTok's median video has 1 view, and 8 of its 21 videos report 0 views.

Five posts have been published since the previous report: four on Instagram and the first TikTok video in 48 days. Two Instagram reels about the Xi'an corporate training reached 15,931 and 11,888 views and immediately joined the account's most-viewed posts.

Those two breakouts earned almost no response — 1.6 and 0.4 engagements per 1,000 views against an Instagram median of 11.2 — and the newest post, a memorial reel, has 45 views and 0 engagement, the lowest reach on the account.
The 2026 AI-skills period still outperforms 2025 on every typical measure: a median of 365.5 views and 23.7 engagements per 1,000 (40 posts) against 210 and 6.1 in 2025 (30 posts).

Judged against the previous report's five recommended tests, four were not tried — none of the new posts uses a recommended format — and the TikTok restart was only partially run: a single video, not the recommended tool-choice format or daily rhythm, at 44 views against the 100-view pass mark.
Cadence remains the structural weakness: Instagram has posted in 19 weeks across a 399-day span, including a 178-day silence, and TikTok's 21 videos have appeared in just 2 active weeks.

instagram.text: This is a reach-and-breakout channel. A typical post gets 312.5 views, 15 reels have passed 1,000 views, and the top 4 reels hold 60% of Instagram views. The two newest reels — both about the Xi'an corporate training — reached 15,931 and 11,888 views.

Engagement is thin in absolute terms: the median post has 4 likes and 0 comments, and only 25 of the 70 posts have any comment at all. Shares are not public on Instagram, so engagement here is likes plus comments.

Reach and response have decoupled in the newest posts. The Xi'an reels earned 1.6 and 0.4 engagements per 1,000 views — far below the Instagram median of 11.2 — and the latest post, a memorial reel, has 45 views and 0 engagement.
The account has improved since the pivot to AI-skills content: 2026 posts median 365.5 views and 23.7 engagements per 1,000 (40 posts), against 210 and 6.1 in 2025 (30 posts).
Because the AI-topic pivot and the calendar change coincide, part of the 2026 lift may reflect account growth over time rather than content alone. This dataset cannot separate the two.

Posting is bursty: 70 posts across 19 active weeks in a 399-day span, with a 178-day silence between December 2025 and June 2026. The latest burst — three reels within minutes of each other on 5 October — included two of the account's biggest reach posts, so same-hour stacking did not cap their distribution.

tiktok.text: The channel has resumed, barely. The first 20 videos went out across 17–20 August 2026 to an account with 2 followers; 8 of them report 0 views. After a 48-day silence, one new video went up hours before this report: 44 views, 0 likes and 1 save.

Judged against the previous report's TikTok test — a natively posted tool-choice video, then one a day for a week, passing at a 100-view weekly median — the restart is partial: the script is new rather than reused from Instagram, but the format is a quote-hook explainer, the daily rhythm has not happened, and 44 views is below the pass mark.
The best day remains 20 August: 4 of the 5 videos posted that day reached 151–224 views, and those four hold all 25 likes the account has received. Only 5 videos in total have passed 100 views.

A burst of 20 uploads from a brand-new account, most reusing Instagram captions, may have limited early distribution. Public data cannot confirm how TikTok treated these uploads; check TikTok Studio for restriction or 'ineligible for For You' notices before the next push.

differences.text: TikTok's pooled engagement rate (25.2 per 1,000 views) sits above Instagram's (13.2), but it rests on 991 total views and 25 likes. It is a small-number artefact, not evidence that TikTok audiences engage more.
Across the 16 scripts posted to both platforms, the median result was 405.5 views on Instagram and 1 view on TikTok.

Where TikTok did get views, the strongest videos were an AI tool-choice script (224 views, 9 likes, 3 saves), a 'stop using AI like a search engine' how-to (221 views, 7 likes, 2 saves) and an ROI story about investing $80 in skills (210 views, 6 likes) — the same themes that engage best on Instagram.
The platforms are at different stages rather than one being 'better': Instagram has 2,237 followers and an algorithm history; TikTok has 2 followers and neither.

ig_DbX5MjSpBJq.text: Highest views (37,467) and by far the highest engagement: 1,735 likes, 0 comments, 46.3 per 1,000 views. It holds 68% of all Instagram likes.
It combines a second-person question hook, a statistic and a career-gap stakes line.

The like count is so far above every other post (the next best has 114) that an external push — a boost, a share by a large account or a feature — is plausible. Public data cannot confirm whether it was boosted, so check Instagram Insights → 'Reach from ads'.

ig_DaRlBaKJboP.text: Second-highest reach (37,449 views) but only 84 engagements, or 2.2 per 1,000 views — well below the Instagram median rate of 11.2.

The 'Imagine an AI that…' hook earns the watch, but the caption gives no reason to respond: no question, poll or save prompt. That fits the wider curiosity-hook pattern of high reach and low response.

ig_DbeIUn4zOmf.text: The caption is only hashtags ('#movitation #success #businesswomen'), yet the reel reached 28,524 views — 145.2× the median of other mindset posts — with 114 likes (4 per 1,000).

The caption cannot explain this result. Whatever worked is in the video itself (visual, audio or on-screen text), which this dataset does not capture. Review the video directly before trying to repeat it.

ig_DeGjopBp3zE.text: New since the previous report: a personal-story reel about the Xi'an training ('My client didn't just say thank you…') reached 15,931 views — the account's fourth-highest — but earned 26 likes and 0 comments, or 1.6 per 1,000.
Client-story content may travel on the strength of the event rather than the caption; with no question or takeaway, viewers had nothing to respond to.

ig_DeGjbgXpL0k.text: Posted within minutes of two other Xi'an reels, it still reached 11,888 views with only 5 engagements (4 likes, 1 comment), or 0.4 per 1,000 — the clearest case of reach without response in the dataset, and evidence that same-hour stacking did not prevent distribution this time.

ig_DeIyuCspe1t.text: The newest Instagram post — a memorial reel for Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali — has 45 views and 0 engagement, the lowest reach on the account.
A one-off memorial post sits outside the account's AI-training positioning, which may have limited its distribution; the dataset cannot confirm the cause.

ig_DZrioHUpxkY.text: A 64-second reel with a one-line caption ('AI isn't coming. Is already here') reached 13,955 views and 111 engagements — 22.5× the median for its topic.
As with the hashtag-only reel, the video content rather than the caption probably drove reach.

ig_DZrwCzEpUB3.text: Best engagement rate among above-median posts: 58.6 per 1,000 views, with 11 comments — the most comments on any post in the dataset — on 666 views.
It promotes a specific in-person class (day, place, format). Concrete, local offers may prompt questions in a way that generic course promotion does not.

ig_DbcsbITpyVi.text: Instagram reports 283 plays but 15,523 legacy 'video views' for this reel, alongside 66 likes and 3 comments. The two view fields normally move together, so treat its 243.8 per-1,000 rate with caution.

ig_Dahb9AMJXry.text: The quiz hook reached 6,805 views but earned 6 likes and 0 comments — 0.9 per 1,000, one of the lowest rates among high-reach posts.
A quiz invites an answer, but the caption answers it immediately. Asking viewers to comment their answer first might convert this reach.

tt_7693746667119578374.text: The first TikTok video in 48 days — a fresh script framing the gap between using and deploying AI as $200,000 in salary savings — has 44 views, 0 likes and 1 save, and its numbers are only hours old.
That is above the account median of 1 view but below the 100-view pass mark the previous report set for the TikTok restart test.

tt_7675946301724314898.text: Best TikTok video: 224 views, 9 likes and 3 saves — 40.2 per 1,000. The same script also beat the median on Instagram (409 views, 36.7 per 1,000 there).

tt_7675200156626849044.text: Same script as the top Instagram reel (37,467 views there), but 1 view on TikTok.
This remains the clearest evidence that TikTok's problem is distribution rather than content quality.

tt_7676052264208928018.text: A TikTok-only how-to ('Stop using AI like a search engine') reached 221 views, 7 likes and 2 saves — 31.7 per 1,000.

topicNotes.ai-how-to: Highest median reach on Instagram (5,313.5 views across 6 posts) but a low engagement rate (6.3 per 1,000). This content attracts viewers without getting them to respond. On TikTok, the topic's best video reached 221 views.
topicNotes.ai-future-of-work: Holds the #1 post (37,467 views). A typical Instagram post gets 621 views and 18.4 engagements per 1,000 (7 posts). On TikTok, all 5 posts had 5 views or fewer.
topicNotes.ai-tool-choice: The most consistent performer: 387 median views and 30.9 engagements per 1,000 on Instagram (5 posts), and it produced the best TikTok video (224 views, 9 likes, 3 saves).
topicNotes.course-promo: The most-used topic (24 posts across both platforms; 17 on Instagram). A typical Instagram post engages well per view (26.5 per 1,000) but is capped at 302 median views — except when it is not: the two new Xi'an training reels reached 15,931 and 11,888 views, the topic's best results, though at 1.6 and 0.4 per 1,000 they barely engaged.
topicNotes.corporate-escape: The 2025 topic with the most reach: 2,256 median views over 5 posts, but a low engagement rate (5.5 per 1,000). It has not been used since the AI pivot.
topicNotes.work-life-balance: Median 203 views over 8 posts; one question-led outlier reached 5,941 views with only 6 engagements (1 per 1,000).
topicNotes.mindset: The largest topic (14 Instagram posts) and the weakest typical result: 196.5 median views, 4.5 per 1,000. The exceptions are a hashtag-only reel at 28,524 views — and, at the other end, the new memorial reel at 45 views, the account's lowest.
topicNotes.travel-bts: Steady but modest: 319 median views, 7.4 per 1,000 (6 posts). Two Riyadh captions read like production notes rather than audience-facing copy.
topicNotes.personal-seasonal: Only 2 posts — a family carousel and a Mid-Autumn Festival image — too few to judge. Neither has a public view count; they earned 9 and 2 likes.

reach-engage.interpretation: Posts that both travelled and got a response: 24 of the 68 scored Instagram posts, and 19 of the 24 are from the 2026 AI period. Note that the Instagram engagement benchmark is only 6 likes plus comments. On TikTok, 13 of the 21 videos land in this quadrant, but with platform medians of 1 view and 0 engagement the TikTok labels are not meaningful.
reach-engage.action: Treat these as templates. Re-cut the winning scripts with new examples rather than inventing new formats.

reach-only.interpretation: Seen but not acted on: 10 posts, split evenly between 2025 and 2026. The newest member is the 11,888-view Xi'an reel, which earned 5 engagements (0.4 per 1,000) — the extreme case of this pattern.
reach-only.action: Keep the format and give the viewer something to do: a point of view to agree or disagree with, a save-worthy takeaway, or a direct question at the end.

engage-only.interpretation: A small audience that liked what it saw: 11 posts, 9 of them from 2026. Seven of the eleven are course-promotion posts: existing followers respond, but the posts rarely travel past a few hundred views.
engage-only.action: Do not expect reach from promotion. Pair each promotional post with a reach post (a question or curiosity hook on AI and careers), and re-post the strongest promotional post with an outcome-led first line.

neither.interpretation: 23 posts, 18 of them from 2025 — mostly the September–October 2025 mindset and work-life-balance reels, many posted in same-day batches with near-identical scripts. The new memorial reel (45 views, 0 engagement) is the latest addition.
neither.action: Retire short aphorism reels as a stand-alone format, and keep off-topic posts rare.

lines.text: Wednesday has the highest median views among well-sampled days (511.5, 14 posts). Friday posts earn the most engagement per 1,000 views (30.1, 11 posts), followed by Monday (18, 15 posts).
Each weekday has only 6 to 15 posts, and Sunday (3 posts) is low-sample. Day of week is not a reliable lever in this dataset.

Evening posts (Kuala Lumpur time) have the highest median reach on Instagram among well-sampled slots: 402 views (15 posts), against 332.5 in the afternoon (32 posts) and 210 at night (18 posts); evening also has the highest median engagement rate (22.5 per 1,000). Evening leads the well-sampled slots in both the 2025 and 2026 periods, so the result is not only a side-effect of topic. Morning is low-sample (5 posts).
TikTok's time-of-day differences are confounded with the day the account started getting views (20 August), so they are not used.

On Instagram, 40–59-second reels keep the best balance: 371 median views and the highest engagement rate, 25 per 1,000 (19 posts). Under-20-second reels are weakest (206 views, 8.9 per 1,000, 14 posts); most of those are 2025 quote reels, so topic and length overlap.

Reels over 60 seconds have become the reach format in 2026: a median of 11,888 views across 9 posts, lifted by the two new Xi'an reels — but at 4 engagements per 1,000 they are the weakest group for response.

AI-related Instagram posts have a median of 371 views and 25 engagements per 1,000 (35 posts); non-AI posts have 212 and 6 (33 posts). AI topics and the 2026 period coincide almost perfectly, so part of this gap may reflect account growth over time.

Instagram posts published within 3 hours of another post now median 313 views (39 posts), essentially identical to stand-alone posts at 312 (29 posts), though their engagement rate is lower (9.8 vs 13.8 per 1,000). The two breakout Xi'an reels were posted within minutes of each other, so same-hour stacking clearly did not cap their reach.
The account still posts in bursts: 3.7 posts per active week on Instagram and 10.5 on TikTok, with long silences in between.

hookNotes.text: On Instagram, hooks still sort into reach hooks and response hooks. Curiosity (median 3,602.5 views, 4 posts — low sample) and question openers (2,256, 7 posts) reach furthest but earn little (3.6 and 1.8 per 1,000). Problem (29.2 per 1,000, 267 median views) and benefit openers (20.9, 345) earn the most per view but reach only a few hundred views.

Question hooks are boom-or-bust: the group contains the best post in the dataset (37,467 views, 46.3 per 1,000) and several posts with 0 engagement, which is why its pooled rate (36.2) and its median rate (1.8) disagree.

Bold claims remain the house style (20 of 70 Instagram posts) and land in the middle: 231.5 median views, 22.4 per 1,000. Inspirational quotes are weakest on both measures (204 views, 4.9 per 1,000, 13 posts) — though the new Xi'an reel shows a quote-style opener can still travel when the event is strong (11,888 views, 0.4 per 1,000).

Pairing a reach hook with a response ending — a question or curiosity opener followed by a 'comment your answer' prompt — may capture both. The top post already does something similar: a question plus a statistic plus stakes.
Hooks were classified from each caption's first line. The spoken or on-screen opening of each video may differ.

more.title: AI career-stakes posts built like the top reel
more.detail: 'Your boss is using AI…' remains the account's benchmark: 37,467 views, 1,735 likes and 46.3 engagements per 1,000, holding 68% of all Instagram likes. The future-of-work topic around it is solid: a typical Instagram post gets 621 views and 18.4 engagements per 1,000 (7 posts). Nothing in this format has been posted since the previous report.

more.title: AI tool-choice comparisons
more.detail: Still the most consistent topic: 387 median views and 30.9 engagements per 1,000 across 5 Instagram posts, and it produced the best TikTok video (224 views, 9 likes, 3 saves). Untried since the previous report.

more.title: Concrete, local class offers
more.detail: The post promoting a specific in-person class earned 39 engagements on 666 views (58.6 per 1,000) and 11 comments — still the most comments on any post in the dataset. A typical course-promotion post gets 302 views (17 Instagram posts), so the concrete offer also travelled further than usual.

more.title: Client and event stories — with an ending that asks for a response
more.detail: The two new Xi'an training reels are course-promotion's best reach results: 15,931 and 11,888 views, the former the account's fourth-highest. Two posts from one event is a thin base, and both earned almost nothing per view (1.6 and 0.4 per 1,000 against a topic median of 26.5). The reach is proven; the missing half is a question or takeaway worth responding to.

less.title: Stand-alone quote and aphorism reels
less.detail: Quote hooks remain the weakest group on both measures: 204 median views and 4.9 engagements per 1,000 (13 posts). The three lowest-reach reels on the account — 45, 74 and 103 views — are all quote-style posts, and the newest of them, the memorial reel, has 45 views and 0 engagement. The one exception is the quote-style Xi'an reel (11,888 views), where the event carried the post.

less.title: Generic course promotion as the default post
less.detail: Course promotion is still the most-used topic (24 posts across both platforms, 17 on Instagram). A typical Instagram promo engages well per view (26.5 per 1,000) but is capped at 302 median views; the only promos to travel further were the Xi'an event stories. Keep promotion a minority of the mix, and make it story-led when it does run.

less.title: Captions that are production notes
less.detail: Two Riyadh posts still carry internal copy ('Vivid language that mirrors your stunning night visuals…'); neither earned more than 2 engagements. Audit captions before publishing.

less.title: Stacking posts minutes apart
less.detail: The reach argument against stacking is gone: posts published within 3 hours of another now median 313 views, essentially identical to stand-alone posts at 312, and the two Xi'an breakouts went out within minutes of each other. But clustered posts still convert less (9.8 vs 13.8 per 1,000), so keep one post per slot for anything that asks for a response.

experiment.title: Job security in the AI era
experiment.detail: Still untested. The 2025 layoff and corporate-exit posts hold the highest median reach of any Instagram topic with 5 or more posts (2,256 views over 5 posts) but a low engagement rate (5.5 per 1,000), and the topic has not been used since the AI pivot. Test it again with an AI-skills angle.

experiment.title: Reels over 60 seconds as a reach play
experiment.detail: The case has strengthened since the previous report: in 2026, reels over 60 seconds median 11,888 views across 9 posts — both Xi'an reels run over 60 seconds — but they earn only 4 engagements per 1,000, the weakest group for response. Test 2–3 more long explainers or event stories with a deliberate response ending rather than making length the default.

experiment.title: Converting curiosity reach into response
experiment.detail: The quiz reel (6,805 views, 6 likes, 0 comments) and 'Imagine an AI…' (37,449 views, 84 engagements, 2.2 per 1,000) had the reach but not the response. Test the same hooks with the answer held back and a 'comment your answer' ending.

hooks.title: For reach: question or curiosity opener
hooks.detail: Question hooks median 2,256 views (7 posts) and curiosity hooks 3,602.5 (4 posts — low sample), but both earn little per view (1.8 and 3.6 per 1,000). Question hooks are boom-or-bust: the group holds the best post in the dataset (37,467 views, 46.3 per 1,000) and posts with 0 engagement, which is why its pooled rate (36.2) and its median rate (1.8) disagree.

hooks.title: For response: problem or benefit opener
hooks.detail: Problem and benefit openers earn the most per view on Instagram (29.2 and 20.9 per 1,000) but reach only a few hundred views (267 and 345 medians). Bold claims — the house style, 20 of 70 posts — sit in the middle on both measures (231.5 views, 22.4 per 1,000).

hooks.title: Combine them
hooks.detail: Open with a question or curiosity line, name the cost in line two, and end with a direct prompt to comment or save. The top post already does a version of this: question plus statistic plus stakes. The two Xi'an reels show the cost of skipping the ending: 15,931 and 11,888 views with almost no response.

duration.title: 40–59 seconds as the default; over-60s as a reach play
duration.detail: The 40–59-second group keeps the best balance on Instagram: 371 median views and the highest engagement rate, 25 per 1,000 (19 posts). Under-20-second reels are weakest (206 views, 8.9 per 1,000, 14 posts), though most of those are 2025 quote reels, so topic and length overlap. Reels over 60 seconds are now the reach format in 2026 — a median of 11,888 views across 9 posts, lifted by the Xi'an reels — but at 4 per 1,000 they convert worst, so reserve length for reach pieces and add a response ending.

posting.title: Post in the evening (Kuala Lumpur time)
posting.detail: Evening posts have the highest median Instagram reach among well-sampled slots: 402 views (15 posts), against 332.5 in the afternoon (32 posts) and 210 at night (18 posts), and the highest median engagement rate (22.5 per 1,000). Evening leads the well-sampled slots in both the 2025 and 2026 periods, so the result is not only a side-effect of topic. Morning has only 5 posts, so it cannot be judged.

posting.title: Keep a steady rhythm; one post per slot
posting.detail: Instagram has posted in only 19 weeks across a 399-day span, including a 178-day silence, and TikTok's 21 videos have appeared in just 2 active weeks. Stacking is no longer a reach concern — clustered posts median 313 views against 312 for stand-alone posts, and the Xi'an breakouts were posted minutes apart — but clustered posts earn less per view (9.8 vs 13.8 per 1,000).

posting.title: Aim for 3–4 posts per week
posting.detail: This is general practice, not derived from this dataset, which has too few steady weeks to identify an optimal frequency.

instagram.title: Role: reach and lead generation
instagram.detail: Instagram holds the audience (2,237 followers) and essentially all of the views (197,763 of 198,754). 24 of the 68 scored posts both travelled and earned a response, and 19 of the 24 are from the 2026 AI period. Optimise for that group: re-cut the winning structures with new examples, and add response endings to curiosity hooks and event stories.

instagram.title: Measure the right thing
instagram.detail: Shares and saves are not public on Instagram, so export them from Instagram Insights to complete the engagement picture, and check 'Reach from ads' on the 37,467-view reel to see whether its 1,735 likes had paid support.

tiktok.title: Role: a restart that has barely begun
tiktok.detail: 21 videos, 2 followers, a median of 1 view and 8 zero-view videos. After 48 days of silence, one new video went up hours before this report: 44 views, 0 likes and 1 save — above the account median, but below the 100-view pass mark set for the restart test, and posted alone rather than as part of a daily rhythm.

tiktok.title: Post natively and on a steady rhythm
tiktok.detail: One video a day for about 3 weeks, filmed or edited in TikTok, starting with the themes that already worked there: tool choice (224 views), 'stop using AI like a search engine' (221) and the $80 ROI story (210).

tiktok.title: Check account health first
tiktok.detail: In TikTok Studio, confirm the 8 zero-view videos are not flagged or restricted before posting more.

nextFive.brief: Carried over from the previous report — still untried, as none of the five posts published since uses this format. Reuse the top-post structure: open with a second-person question ('Your team lead just automated half their week — are you still doing it manually?'), add one statistic, the career-gap stakes, and one concrete skill.
nextFive.measure: Beat 312.5 views (the Instagram median) and 11.2 engagements per 1,000 views (the Instagram median rate).

nextFive.brief: Carried over — untried. 'ChatGPT is the wrong tool for 3 of these 5 jobs.' Show a side-by-side for each job and end with 'save this for your next project'.
nextFive.measure: Views above 387 and engagement per 1,000 views above 30.9 (the topic medians).

nextFive.brief: Carried over — untried. Rerun the AI vs AI agent vs agentic AI quiz, but hold the answer: 'Comment A, B or C before the reveal.'
nextFive.measure: More than 11 comments would make it the most-commented post on the account; the original earned 0 comments on 6,805 views.

nextFive.brief: Carried over — untried. Bring back the 2025 layoff angle with an AI-skills twist: 'Banks cut 3,500 jobs by email. Here is the skill that makes you the person they keep.'
nextFive.measure: Instagram views above 2,256 (the layoff-topic median); on TikTok, above 224 views (the best TikTok video so far).

nextFive.brief: Partially attempted since the previous report: the 7 October video used a fresh script, but not the tool-choice format or the daily rhythm, and finished at 44 views against the 100-view pass mark. Run the full test: a new, natively filmed version of the best TikTok video ('Not all AI is built equal'), posted alone on a quiet day, then one video a day for a week.
nextFive.measure: Median TikTok views for the week above 100; the account median today is 1.
